extracted.intended_audience: U.S. employers, immigration practitioners, HR professionals, unions, and other stakeholders in PERM, H-1B/H-1B1/E-3 labor certification and prevailing wage rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Labor Notice of Proposed Rulemaking revising the prevailing wage methodology for PERM and LCAs (H-1B, H-1B1, E-3). The page provides the proposed regulatory text, background, statutory framework, instructions for public comments, and request for input on alternatives and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission content and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be confined to issues pertinent to the NPRM, identify the agency's name and public docket number ETA-2026-0001, explain the reasons for any recommended changes, and reference the specific section and wording being addressed, where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit electronically via Regulations.gov; include docket number; explain reasons for recommended changes and cite specific sections/wording when possible. The Department will post comments to Regulations.gov after review. Deadline for comments: May 26, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public nature of comments and sensitive information guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments are considered public and will be posted online once the Labor Department has reviewed them. The Department may redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit trade secrets, confidential/proprietary commercial or financial information, personal health information, sensitive PII (e.g., SSN, driver's license, passport, financial account numbers), or information you do not want made public. Agency may redact or refrain from posting comments containing such information; depending on submission method, the agency may be unable to redact and may instead refuse to post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of agency's request for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department requests comments on all aspects of its revised methodology for establishing prevailing wage levels and regulatory alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency explicitly solicits input on methodology steps, percentile choices, implementation, reliance interests, and enumerated regulatory alternatives (see other rubric entries). Respondents should address any aspect of the revised methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: LCA employer wage and working-conditions attestations
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer is offering and will offer wages that are at least the actual wage paid by the employer to individuals with similar experience and qualifications or the prevailing wage as determined by the Department, whichever is greater, and will provide working conditions that will not adversely affect the working conditions of U.S. workers similarly employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attestation is required on LCAs for H-1B, H-1B1, and E-3 filings. Employers must base the prevailing wage on permitted sources and ensure offered wage meets the greater of actual wage or prevailing wage as of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: LCA additional attestations (strike/lockout and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the LCA an employer must attest: (1) there is no strike or lockout in the course of a labor dispute in the occupational classification at the worksite; and (2) it has provided notice of its filing of an LCA to its employees' bargaining representative or posted notice to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice may be by conspicuous posting at the worksite or other means such as electronic notification when no bargaining representative exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rule for prevailing wage determination for LCAs
rubrics_metrics.description: As relevant here, the prevailing wage must be determined as of the time the LCA is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must ensure the source and computation of the prevailing wage correspond to the filing date of the LCA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted sources for LCA prevailing wage
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer may base the prevailing wage on: an applicable CBA negotiated at arm's length; a PWD from the OFLC; a Davis-Bacon Act or Service Contract Act wage determination; an independent authoritative source (e.g., private wage survey) that satisfies 20 CFR requirements; or another legitimate source meeting the regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private wage surveys and other sources must meet the regulatory criteria in 20 CFR 655.731(b)(3)(iii)(B)-(C). The Department may review and reject private surveys that do not meet established criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on filing LCAs before start date
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer may not file an LCA more than six months prior to their selected start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure LCA filing date is within six months of intended employment start date to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: LCA certification timing by Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Secretary finds the LCA is incomplete or obviously inaccurate, the Secretary must certify it within seven working days of its filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers can expect quick certification unless deficiencies are apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: PERM: requirement that employer show no able/willing/qualified U.S. workers and no adverse effect on wages/conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To issue a labor certification, the Secretary of Labor must determine that there are not sufficient able, willing, and qualified workers available at the time of application and that the hiring of the alien worker will not adversely affect the wages or working conditions of workers in the United States similarly employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory standard governs PERM determinations and requires recruitment and documentation by the employer demonstrating the labor market test and lawful rejections of U.S. applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: PERM: Prevailing Wage Determination (PWD) requirement before filing Form ETA-9089
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing a labor certification application, the employer first must obtain a Prevailing Wage Determination (PWD) for its job opportunity from the Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWD standards and procedures are at 20 CFR 656.40 and 656.41. The PWD identifies the wage and validity period (no less than 90 days and no more than one year from determination date).

rubrics_metrics.name: PERM: Employer recruitment, documentation, and attestations on Form ETA-9089
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing Form ETA-9089 the employer must include the labor or services, actual minimum job requirements from the valid PWD, the wage offered, geographic location(s), efforts to recruit qualified and available U.S. workers, and attest that the offered wage equals or exceeds the prevailing wage and that the job was clearly open to any U.S. worker and U.S. applicants were rejected for lawful, job-related reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFLC reviews ETA-9089 and may grant or deny. A granted permanent labor certification is valid only for the job opportunity, employer, alien, and area named and must be used to support an I-140 within 180 calendar days of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: If job covered by CBA, CBA wage is prevailing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the job opportunity is covered by an applicable collective bargaining agreement that was negotiated at arm's length, the wage rate set forth in the CBA is considered the prevailing wage for labor certification purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers should submit the CBA when it applies to the job opportunity to establish prevailing wage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default to OEWS when no other prevailing-wage source available
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a prevailing wage rate derived from an applicable CBA, DBA/SCA determination, or compliant private survey, the OFLC will use the BLS OEWS survey to determine the prevailing wage for the job opportunity based on the most specific occupation and geographic area available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEWS is the Department's primary wage source for detailed geography/occupation; employers should expect OEWS-based determinations when other sources are unavailable or insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-tier unified prevailing wage structure (purpose and application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department applies a unified four-tier prevailing wage structure across PERM and LCA programs, differentiating wages based on education, experience, and level of supervision: Level I corresponds to entry-level roles, Level IV represents the most experienced and highly skilled positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unified structure ensures consistency across temporary and permanent programs and is implemented through ETA regulations (20 CFR parts 655 and 656).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical percentile mapping of four wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department historically applied a formula to set Levels I through IV at approximately the 17th percentile, the 34th percentile, the 50th percentile, and the 67th percentile of the OEWS wage distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical mapping originated from earlier two-tier OEWS calculations and the 2005 Guidance expanding to four levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed methodology steps for revising prevailing wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's proposed revisions involve: Step 1—The Department's analysis of LCA data; Step 2—Comparing the LCA data to general labor market data; Step 3—Using the labor market analysis to revise the prevailing wage system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM includes mathematical details behind Step 2 and explains the Department's rationale for setting particular percentiles for wage levels (see related rubric entries on percentile choices). Comments are invited on all steps and the mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed percentile settings for wage levels (specific proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The document describes the Department's setting of Wage Level I to the 34th percentile and Wage Level IV to the 88th percentile (with Wage Levels II and III set between those benchmarks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM explains interpolation methods (e.g., how to compute the 34th percentile between reported OEWS percentiles) and invites comment on these percentile choices and their implementation across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OEWS data scope and definitional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: OEWS wage estimates are straight-time, gross pay (including piece rates) and exclude overtime, shift differentials, non-production or year-end bonuses; OEWS covers wage and salary workers in nonfarm establishments and excludes self-employed, owners/partners in unincorporated firms, household workers, and unpaid family workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM explains how OEWS data are collected, geographic and occupational granularity, and limitations relevant to constructing prevailing wages and interpreting percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and cross-program consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's unified four-tier methodology is required by the INA and implemented through ETA regulations to ensure prevailing wages are commensurate with experience, education, and supervision across PERM and LCA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking cites statutory authority and explains the need to prevent wage-setting disparities across related programs (PERM, H-1B, H-1B1, E-3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department's right to review/reject private wage surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: 20 CFR 656.40(b)(3) and 655.731(a)(2)(ii)(B)-(C) authorize the Department to review and reject private surveys that do not meet established criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private surveys used to establish prevailing wage must comply with regulatory standards; the proposed rule includes discussion of alternatives (e.g., eliminating private surveys) and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for comment on enumerated regulatory alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM lists regulatory alternatives and requests comment, including: Alternative 1: Using experience benchmarking for adjusting wage levels; Alternative 2: Eliminate the ability to use private wage surveys; Alternative 3: National wage standard for remote and distributed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should provide evidence, reasoning, and suggested wording if they support any alternative; reference specific regulatory sections when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative analyses and required reviews in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM includes and is subject to multiple administrative analyses and Executive Orders: Executive Order 12866 (Regulatory Planning and Review), Executive Order 13563 (Improving Regulation), Executive Order 14192, Regulatory Flexibility Act, Paperwork Reduction Act, Executive Orders on federalism and tribal consultation, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department analyzes costs, benefits, transfer payments, impacts on small entities, paperwork burdens, alternatives, and other statutorily or executive-ordered requirements as part of rulemaking and includes those analyses in the NPRM for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: PERM certification validity and use limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent labor certification is valid only for the job opportunity, employer, alien worker, and area of intended employment named on the Form ETA-9089 and must be filed in support of a Form I-140 petition within 180 calendar days of the date on which OFLC granted the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must adhere to the 180-day filing window and the specificity limits of the certification to avoid invalid petitions.
